operator_signal: Banked follow-up (c) of the view-switch record 20260928-233000 (bench 5777f3bc): 'the refresh_stats round-trip defer (~20ms; TS does not block its first frame on it)' — re-measured at the current tip FIRST, honest negative allowed.
hypothesis: The TUI open path (and every agents-view switch re-entry) blocks its first frame on a get_session_stats daemon round-trip whose only consumer is the tray's context-usage row; the port's AgentConnectionState.context_usage field exists on the wire but was always None (the port's gap vs TS createAgentConnectionState, which carries contextUsage on every attach), so the first frame could be fed off the attach snapshot and the blocking fetch deleted.
approach: MEASURE FIRST at the tip e3870216079 (same-VM sequential, sha-asserted arms, pty 120x40 raw-drain driver, per-leg key->needle->settle walls, spin calibration pre/mid/post, fleet I/O probe battery at every phase boundary): (1) re-measure (3 trials/class); (2) env-gated instr re-decompose (tip+instr vs cut+instr, phase notes t_open_done/t_stats_done/t_rebind_done/t_draw + w_attach_enter/w_msgs/w_attach_done/w_stats_req); (3) the cut (10 files: pa-daemon connection_state_locked fills context_usage via session_stats::store_context_usage under the attach's core lock; pa-tui reconstruct reads state.contextUsage via ContextUsage::from_wire; attach_session applies it with the other reconstructed fields; the blocking refresh_stats deleted from interactive/run.rs's open path + /new + /switch; the settled-turn and post-compaction refreshes kept); (4) interleaved ABBA tip,cut,cut,tip,tip,cut x3 blocks/class (18 trials/class) + pyte-fed controls.

parity_notes: TS createAgentConnectionState carries contextUsage: session.getContextUsage() in EVERY attach snapshot (snapshot.ts:56) and TS's open path never blocks its first frame on getSessionStats (refreshConnectionContextUsage fires only on turn-complete/compaction-end, interactive-mode.ts:6345/6377; the tray's first-frame value is read off connectionState, + the in-flight optimistic delta). The cut restores exactly that mechanism: the wire field is filled (additive; the field existed, always None; older readers ignore it; the daemon and TUI ship as one binary), the blocking fetch is deleted from the open path and the /new + /switch rebinds, and the settled-turn/post-compaction refreshes are untouched. The tray bytes are identical (the oracle above) — the same numbers, the same frames. TUI-output bytes, session-JSONL replay, compaction content, RLM schemas, prompts: untouched. Disclosed adjacent-surface changes: the supersede-rebind and the recovery reattach now also update the tray from their attach snapshots (the same values the removed fetch would have returned; today they keep the previous snapshot's value until the next settled turn — the cut is the tighter TS parity). PR #3303 overlap: NONE (it touches pa-core kernel provisioner + kernel tests; this lane touches the tray-stats surfaces only) — disclosed per the staged-lane convention; no staging needed.
